market_brief: Sunday adds one new risk to Friday's damage: Reuters reports the SEC's Nvidia probe is focused on possible accounting irregularities, after a week in which Nvidia fell 23% (worst since 2008) and the SOX lost 10.7% in a day and 17% on the week. Futures reopen at 6pm ET from Friday's last prints near S&P 6,935 and NDX 25,127, with the VIX at 35.9 and only 117 of 507 S&P names up on Friday. Bonds remain the hedge (10Y 4.91%, -14bp d/d, -24bp w/w) even as futures still price roughly 94% odds of a December Fed hike; gold (-4.6% to ~$3,515), silver (-7.3%) and Brent (~$90 Feb) were sold, and bitcoin slipped back under $59k Sunday after reclaiming $60k. Asia carries the most risk into Monday after Taiwan (-17.5% w/w), Kospi and Nikkei each lost 5-6% Friday, while India is the outlier with Nifty at a nine-month-high close of 25,800 (+2.6% w/w, Bank Nifty +5.9%) and 26,000 as resistance. Thanksgiving week brings HPE and Zoom on Monday, PCE and GDP mid-week, a US holiday Thursday and the OPEC+ 2027 quota meeting on Nov 29.
ai_brief: Weekend AI news is mostly deals and open models rather than flagship launches: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, a small Apache-2.0 open-weights coding model, and Amazon is reportedly close to buying video-AI startup Decart for about $7.5B. At the UN, 128 countries agreed to elaborate possible rules on autonomous weapons by 2028, stopping short of a ban. Newsletters remain focused on Anthropic's choppy first week as a public company, Nvidia's leadership and regulatory troubles, and GPT-6.2's mixed reception.

items.headline: Reuters: SEC's Nvidia probe centres on potential accounting irregularities
items.summary: Two people briefed told Reuters that SEC enforcement staff are scrutinising possible accounting issues at Nvidia; earlier reports confirmed a probe but not its focus. The stock fell 14% Friday and 23% on the week, its worst week since October 2008, and the DOJ is separately reviewing its $12.9B Hugging Face deal.

items.headline: Geographic revenue reporting may be in SEC's sights; Nvidia trades near 8x forward earnings
items.summary: A Motley Fool analysis notes Nvidia changed how it attributes China revenue (from billing address to customer headquarters), reporting $19.7B from China-headquartered customers in fiscal 2026, which it suggests could interest regulators. It adds that roughly $1T of market value was lost in the week and that investigations could weigh for months.

items.headline: Futures reopen Sunday 6pm ET from S&P 6,935 and NDX 25,127 last prints; breadth was 117 up, 390 down
items.summary: Friday's last futures prints were S&P 500 -3.6%, Nasdaq 100 -5.5% and Russell 2000 -2.9%. Nebius and SanDisk lost about 16% each in the cash session, while Global Payments rose about 10% as one of few gainers.

items.headline: December Fed hike odds ease to ~94% from near-certainty as stocks slide
items.summary: Investing.com's futures-based monitor showed a 93.6% chance of a December hike on Nov 20, down from 99.6% a day earlier. The 10Y yield fell 14bp to 4.91% Friday as Treasuries, not gold, acted as the haven.

items.headline: Anthropic's five published price targets average $134 versus an $88.91 close
items.summary: Targets reported by Reuters range from New Street's $105 to Melius's $155, with Needham at $150, Wolfe at $135 and Citizens at $125; Seaport began at Neutral without a target. Underwriter coverage could begin around Nov 30 once the quiet period lapses, though no bank has said so.

items.headline: PBoC holds loan prime rates for an 18th straight month
items.summary: China left its one- and five-year LPRs unchanged in November, keeping the one-year rate at 3.00%, even as mainland and Hong Kong stocks slid to their lowest since mid-2025.

items.headline: Brent heads into OPEC+ 2027 quota meeting after a third weekly fall
items.summary: January Brent settled at $92.57 Friday (-3.4% on the week) and WTI at $83.41, as easing Hormuz flows and an expected Q4 surplus weigh. OPEC+ ministers meet Nov 29 to set 2027 output, a day before the January Brent contract expires.

items.headline: Update: bitcoin slips back below $59,000 on Sunday after brief reclaim of $60k
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $58,900 Sunday morning in a $58,700-$60,200 range, giving back part of its rebound from Saturday's ~$55k low. Spot bitcoin ETFs have seen about $2.35B of net outflows in recent sessions.

items.headline: Prediction-market traders bet on where bitcoin sits at Sunday's 16:59 UTC mark
items.summary: Decrypt's prediction-market page lists live contracts on bitcoin's price at 4:59pm UTC on Nov 22, a sign of how closely retail traders are watching the weekend crypto tape ahead of futures reopening.

items.headline: Nifty and Sensex post best closes in nine months; analysts eye 26,000
items.summary: Nifty rose 2.6% on the week to 25,800.6 and Sensex 2.85% to 83,919.7, a fourth straight weekly gain, with Bank Nifty up 5.9% after a record intraday high. The gains were concentrated in large caps while midcaps were flat and smallcaps fell; one analyst puts resistance at 26,000 and support at 25,550.

items.headline: Update: Razorpay and Sembcorp Green Infra listed as cleared by SEBI to launch IPOs
items.summary: SEBI's update showed final observations for Razorpay (Nov 3; issue reportedly ₹5,000-6,000 crore) and Sembcorp Green Infra (Nov 13; up to ₹3,750 crore, all fresh equity). Razorpay is reportedly aiming to list by February 2027.

items.headline: Week ahead: HPE, Zoom, Agilent Monday; PCE and GDP mid-week; holiday-shortened trading
items.summary: HPE, Zoom, Agilent and Symbotic report after Monday's close, followed by Dell and Deere later in the week alongside US PCE and GDP. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shut early (1pm ET) Friday; OPEC+ meets Nov 29.

items.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini open-weights coding model
items.summary: The 26.4B-parameter (3.4B active) model has a 1M-token context and Apache 2.0 licence; the company reports it edging Qwen3.8-27B on SWE-bench Verified and DeepSWE but trailing on Terminal Bench (self-reported).

items.headline: Amazon reportedly nearing ~$7.5B deal for AI video startup Decart
items.summary: Per an FT report, Amazon is in advanced talks to acquire Decart, which was reportedly valued at about $4B in May; no deal has been announced.

items.headline: UN talks: countries agree to work towards rules on 'killer robots' by 2028
items.summary: States at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva agreed to elaborate possible rules on lethal autonomous weapons by 2028, building on a definitional text backed by 128 countries, but without a binding ban.

items.headline: Anthropic closes IPO with greenshoe fully exercised; Amodei eyes investment-grade rating
items.summary: Anthropic's closing notice reportedly covered 1.127B Class A shares at $83 including a fully exercised 147M-share underwriter option. Dario Amodei said the company hopes for an investment-grade rating and future debt financing, describing ~$900B of compute commitments as spread over years.

items.headline: Hassabis responds after SemiAnalysis retracts claim DeepMind lost its edge
items.summary: Demis Hassabis replied light-heartedly after research firm SemiAnalysis apologised for and withdrew a claim about Gemini 4 that suggested DeepMind had fallen behind.

items.headline: NIO to launch NWM 3.0 world model for driving on Nov 25
items.summary: NIO plans to unveil the third version of its NIO World Model at its NIO IN 2026 event on Nov 25, part of a wider push by carmakers into world models for autonomy.

items.headline: Feed focus: Anthropic's record IPO, Nvidia after Huang, GPT-6.2's rough launch
items.summary: Weekly AI newsletters are framing the week around Anthropic's $81B listing and quick give-back, Nvidia's leadership vacuum and probes, and power-user pushback on OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.

items.headline: OpenRouter adds Inkling 2 Mini and a Mistral Pixtral Large build to its catalogue
items.summary: Kilo's open-weight tracker shows Inkling 2 Mini listed on OpenRouter on Nov 21 and Mistral's Pixtral Large 2502 on Nov 20 (catalogue dates, not release dates).
